To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the performance of organizations can be predicted from their structure, that the performance of the organization can be predicted from the performance of the individuals in it, and that the performance of an individual in an organization can be predicted in part from the performance of other individuals in the organization.
organizational researchers are not as stupid as we sometimes seem to think they are, and that the problems of organizational performance are much more complex than we sometimes seem to realize.
organizational performance is a dependent variable, but not a very good one.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the way in which the organizational research community has responded to the problem of causal inference and the way in which this problem is related to the broader issues of the social organization of scientific knowledge.
the way organizational researchers respond to contradictory demands and how they resolve the conflicts between them.
the ways that organizational research can be used to improve organizational performance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the organizational research community is in the process of trying to resolve its dilemmas by a strategy that is neither satisfactory nor inevitable.
the use of performance as a dependent measure is a legitimate and useful approach to the study of performance.
the use of organizational performance as a dependent measure in organizational research is a complex issue.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the study of organizational performance is not yet a mature science.
the study of organizational performance as a dependent measure is an interesting but difficult enterprise that is not likely to be resolved in the near future.
organizational performance is a function of the organizational environment, the organization's internal processes, and the organization itself.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the organizational performance literature has been dominated by a particular approach to the study of organizational performance, one that defines performance as a dependent measure and seeks to identify variables that predict performance.
organizational performance is a dependent variable.
organizational researchers need to be more explicit about the causal inferences they make, and more critical of those made by others.
